title: World History Challenge
intro: From ancient empires to the modern age, a tougher tour of world history beyond the basics.

questions.prompt: Which empire was ruled from the city of Cuzco?
questions.explanation: Cuzco, high in the Andes of Peru, was the Inca capital. Their empire stretched along much of western South America.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor had the Taj Mahal built?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Work began in about 1632.

questions.prompt: The Code of Hammurabi, one of the oldest written law codes, comes from which ancient kingdom?
questions.explanation: King Hammurabi of Babylon had about 282 laws carved on a stone pillar in the 1700s BC.

questions.prompt: Which peace settlement of 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War?
questions.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia was agreed in the towns of Münster and Osnabrück and reshaped the map of Europe.

questions.prompt: Who became the first emperor of a unified China, founding the Qin dynasty?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang united China in 221 BC and standardised writing, coins and weights. He is also known for the Terracotta Army.

questions.prompt: Which empire captured Constantinople in 1453?
questions.explanation: Sultan Mehmed II took the city, ending the Byzantine Empire. It became the Ottoman capital and is now Istanbul.

questions.prompt: Who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, in December 1911?
questions.explanation: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen used dog sleds and reached the Pole about five weeks before Scott's team.

questions.prompt: Mansa Musa, famed for his great wealth, ruled which West African empire?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa ruled Mali in the 1300s. His pilgrimage to Mecca, with huge amounts of gold, made him famous across the world.

questions.prompt: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 began a period of rapid modernisation in which country?
questions.explanation: The Meiji Restoration returned power to the Japanese emperor and transformed Japan into an industrial nation within decades.

questions.prompt: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps with war elephants to invade Italy?
questions.explanation: Hannibal crossed the Alps in 218 BC during the Second Punic War against Rome.

questions.prompt: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World stood at the harbour of Alexandria?
questions.explanation: The Pharos of Alexandria was one of the tallest structures of the ancient world and guided ships for centuries.

questions.prompt: Which king was crowned emperor by the Pope in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800?
questions.explanation: Charlemagne, king of the Franks, ruled much of western Europe. His crowning revived the idea of an emperor in the West.

questions.prompt: The Rosetta Stone carries the same text in hieroglyphs, demotic script and which other language?
questions.explanation: Because scholars could read the Greek, the stone helped Jean-François Champollion crack Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822.

questions.prompt: Which Russian ruler founded the city of St Petersburg in 1703?
questions.explanation: Peter the Great built St Petersburg on the Baltic coast as his 'window on Europe' and made it Russia's capital.

questions.prompt: Simón Bolívar led independence movements across much of which continent?
questions.explanation: Known as 'the Liberator', Bolívar helped free Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia from Spanish rule.

questions.prompt: The Hanseatic League was a powerful trading alliance of towns based mainly around which seas?
questions.explanation: The Hanseatic League, centred on towns such as Lübeck, dominated northern European trade from the 1200s to the 1400s.

questions.prompt: The ancient city of Carthage lay in which modern country?
questions.explanation: Carthage stood on the coast near modern Tunis. It was Rome's great rival until it was destroyed in 146 BC.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.explanation: Octavian took the title Augustus in 27 BC. Julius Caesar held great power but was never emperor.

questions.prompt: Which people built the city of Tenochtitlan, on the site of modern Mexico City?
questions.explanation: The Aztecs (Mexica) built Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in the 1300s, linked to land by causeways.

questions.prompt: Whose expedition of 1519 to 1522 made the first voyage around the world, though he did not survive the journey?
questions.explanation: Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano led the last surviving ship home to Spain.

questions.prompt: Which Florentine writer and diplomat wrote The Prince, a famous book on political power?
questions.explanation: Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513. The word 'Machiavellian', meaning cunning, comes from his name.

questions.prompt: The Silk Road trade routes chiefly linked China with which region?
questions.explanation: For centuries, silk, spices, ideas and religions travelled along the Silk Road between East Asia and the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the first Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC, about 2,500 years later, but under 2,000 years before 1969.

questions.prompt: The Hundred Years' War between England and France lasted exactly 100 years.
questions.explanation: It ran from 1337 to 1453, about 116 years, with long periods of truce in between.

questions.prompt: The Byzantine Empire was the eastern part of the Roman Empire, which carried on for centuries after Rome itself fell.
questions.explanation: Ruled from Constantinople, the Byzantine Empire lasted until 1453, almost a thousand years after the western empire ended.

questions.prompt: Nelson Mandela became president of South Africa in 1994.
questions.explanation: After 27 years in prison, Mandela was elected in South Africa's first fully democratic election in 1994.

questions.prompt: Napoleon Bonaparte was born on the island of Corsica.
questions.explanation: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio, Corsica, in 1769, just a year after the island passed from Genoa to France.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany was reunified the following year.

questions.prompt: In which year did the French Revolution begin with the storming of the Bastille?
questions.explanation: Crowds stormed the Bastille prison in Paris on 14 July 1789, now celebrated as France's national day.

questions.prompt: In which year did the First World War end?
questions.explanation: Fighting stopped with the Armistice on 11 November 1918, remembered each year on Armistice Day.
